chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abdul Aziz ibn Yahya al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Atiye narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Sa'id al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Suleiman, who was a reader of books,

he said: I read in one of the Books of Allah, the Exalted, that when Zul-Qarnayn finished building the dam, he set out on his way. While he was traveling with his troops, he passed by a knowledgeable man. Zul-Qarnayn said to him: Inform me about two things that have been standing since Allah, the Exalted, created them? And about two things that are moving? And about two things that are different? And about two things that are opposite to each other? The knowledgeable man said to Zul-Qarnayn: As for the two standing things, they are the heavens and the earth. As for the two moving things, they are the sun and the moon. As for the two different things, they are the night and the day. As for the two opposite things, they are death and life. He said: Go, for you are knowledgeable. The hadith is long; we have taken from it what is needed, and I have narrated it in full in the Book of Prophethood.

key_terms.السَّدِّ: The Dam, a structure built by Zul-Qarnayn
key_terms.ذُو الْقَرْنَيْنِ: Zul-Qarnayn (The Two-Horned One), a biblical and Quranic figure

ai.seo_question: What are the two standing, two moving, two different, and two opposite things according to the narration of Zul-Qarnayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Zul-Qarnayn demonstrates his profound wisdom by categorizing cosmic phenomena into four distinct relational pairs, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the order and balance (*mizan*) within creation. This dialogue serves as a testament to the continuity of divine knowledge across prophetic traditions, linking the Quranic figure of Zul-Qarnayn to broader eschatological and cosmological themes found in Islamic exegesis.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-80 Abul Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdul Aziz ibn Yahya al-Basry quoted Muhammad ibn Atiye, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Sa’id al-Basry, on the authority of Himad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Suleiman who used to read many books as saying,

“I have read in one of the Books of the Honorable the Exalted God that once Zul-Qarnayn finished building the dam he continued his travels. He ran into a knowledgeable man during his travels with his troops. The knowledgeable man asked him, ‘Let me know about the two things which are standing ever since the Honorable the Exalted God created them, the two things which are moving, the two things which are different from each other and the two things which are opposite of each other.’ Zul-Qarnayn said, ‘The two things which are standing are the heavens and the Earth. The two things which are moving are the sun and the moon. The two things which are differentfrom each other are the day and the night, and the two things which are opposite of each other are life and death.’ The knowledgeable man said, ‘Go. You are knowledgeable.”This tradition is long, but I have only mentioned a short part of it here as deemed necessary. I have narrated it in full in the book Kitab al-Nabuwah.
